compiled_state.title: As a planner, I emit an automated-sweep plus manual-verification task pair for sweep-class changes
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description
**What**: When the persisted marker class is sweep, the dso:task-decomposer emits an automated-sweep task (recipe-preferred, agent-sweep fallback) paired with an agent-driven manual-verification task that checks completeness and semantic correctness.
**Why**: Mechanical repeated changes are automated and then verified, catching missed sites and semantic regressions at plan time.
**Scope**:
- IN: sweep-class emission of the (automated-sweep, manual-verification) pair with the verification done-definition.
- OUT: db rollback pairs; feature-flag pairs; sprint scheduling order.

## Done Definitions
- For a migration-class:sweep change, task-decomposer emits an automated-sweep task whose transform descriptor (recipe rule or sg rewrite) is distinct from the broad detection query, preferring the recipe engine with agent-sweep fallback
  ← Satisfies: sc-2  (sc-2: sweep + verification pair emission)
- The emitted manual-verification task's done-definition requires re-running the detection query and asserting zero remaining sites, with un-automatable sites recorded as inline TODO(migration) markers and enumerated in an un_automatable_sites field
  ← Satisfies: sc-2
- The same manual-verification done-definition requires the test gate to pass over modified files, so a zero detection count without a passing test gate is not treated as complete
  ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
  ← Satisfies: sc-2

## Considerations
- [Maintainability] This story, the db-rollback story, and the feature-flag story all edit the same dso:task-decomposer emission logic. Define a single emission dispatch point keyed on marker class (sweep→sweep pair, db→rollback pair, flag-tag→flag pair) so the stories add cases rather than overwriting one another. Reserve task-type namespaces (automated-sweep, manual-verification, rollback, rollback-verification, flag-cutover, flag-cleanup) to avoid collisions.

## Escalation Policy
**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
